newsitem.title: THAILAND: Growing fast food demand helps Thai KFC.
newsitem.headline: Growing fast food demand helps Thai KFC.

text.p: Convenience is becoming a big business in food-crazed Thailand, and Kentucky Fried Chicken said on Tuesday it has reaped the benefits of changing Thai eating habits and growing disposable income.
The Thai market is among the fastest growing in the world for KFC, with an average annual growth of about 40 percent per year, said Hester Chew, KFC country manager for Thailand and Indochina.

"The whole category of fast food (in Thailand) is growing at about 30 percent a year," Chew told Reuters in an interview. "In Thailand, we have 133 restaurants and we're heading towards 150 by December or January."
KFC hopes to have 300 outlets in Thailand by the turn of the century, and Chew said Thailand's long-term potential is for about 500 branches.
With expected revenues of about $100 million in Thailand this year, KFC is the country's largest fast-food restaurant chain with about a 36 percent market share, Chew said.
The second largest is McDonalds, which has 47 outlets based mainly in Bangkok, he said.

Chew said the capital city is still KFC's main growth area, but the company has also been expanding rapidly in the provinces as more Thais get a taste for fried chicken and as the restaurant adds spicy menu items adapted to the Thai palate.
Fast food popularity is growing in Thailand due to a combination of factors, Chew said.
"Young adults and teenagers have more disposable income and are associating more with Western lifestyles," he said. "There are also more double-income families."
In a country where snack-happy Thais can get a wide variety of cheap and tasty foods at roadside stalls, KFC is working hard to get consumers.

"The whole notion is to create convenience," Chew said. He said KFC has experimented with home delivery, especially in traffic-clogged Bangkok, and also set up an outlet at a petrol filling station for those who want to get a quick bite on the road.
KFC has focused its marketing efforts on the family market, launching a children's club and decorating its restaurants to be more family-oriented with playgrounds and toys.
"Eating out in a restaurant, especially for young families, is an experience," Chew said. "In the States, fast food is probably the cheapest form of food -- you buy it and take it home to eat."
Contrary to Western markets, like the United States, most Asian consumers prefer to eat in fast food restaurants instead of drive through or buy takeout food, he said.

"In Thailand, about 70 percent of people dine in, compared to about 30 percent in the States," he said. "The average seating in a KFC restaurant in the States is about 50 seats, and here it averages 150 seats."
Chew said KFC hopes to make Thailand the base for the Indochina market, which is still in the planning stages. He said KFC hopes to open its first branch in Vietnam next year.
Kentucky Fried Chicken is a unit of PepsiCo Inc's Pepsi Restaurant International.
